title: Oscars Visual Effects Top 20 Revealed: Disney Leads With Four Titles as ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘Ramayana,’ ‘Dune: Part Three’ and ‘Wildwood’ Make the Cut (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Oscars VFX 20-film shortlist favors Disney, boosting visibility for actors in effects-driven releases.
content: Other VFX finalists include “Backrooms,” “Digger,” “Godzilla Minus Zero,” “The Mosquito Bowl,” “Project Hail Mary” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” The Oscar race for visual effects is down to 20, and the road to the 99th Academy Awards runs through Ithaca, Motunui and a galaxy far, far away. The Academy’s Visual Effects Branch notified the artisans behind the 20 films advancing to the next round ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. Through multiple sources, Variety has confirmed all 20 of the finalists, including Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three,” Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” Phil Lord and Christopher Miller’s “Project Hail Mary,” Steven Spielberg’s “Disclosure Day” and Marvel Studios’ “ Avengers: Doomsday ” from Anthony and Joe Russo. Related Stories 'The Body' Debuts With 5.1 Million Views in Five Days 'Heartland' Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir The Academy does not release the top 20 externally and declines to comment or confirm which films advanced. Disney leads the confirmed titles with four. Alongside “Avengers: Doomsday,” the studio lands Jon Favreau’s “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu,” 20th Century Studios’ “Whalefall” and Thomas Kail’s live-action “Moana,” which brings Dwayne Johnson back as the demigod Maui. Skydance (formerly Warner Bros. Discovery) took three of the spots: “Dune: Part Three,” Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s Tom Cruise-led “Digger” and Craig Gillespie’s “Supergirl” from former DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran. But the studio also sees four contenders fall short. Villeneuve’s stakes are historic. Both “Dune” and “Dune: Part Two” won the visual effects Oscar, and in March, “Avatar: Fire and Ash” made James Cameron’s franchise three-for-three in the category. “Dune: Part Three,” which opens Dec. 18, now puts Villeneuve two steps from the same trilogy sweep. title: The Top 21 New Movies Streaming Now
summary: November streaming drops spotlight major new films, offering fresh visibility for featured talent across platforms.
content: Nicolas Cage as John Madden, a Jessica Chastain thriller and the biggest horror movie of the year hit streaming in November If you’re looking for a great new movie to watch on streaming, you’ve come to the right place. November has a host of new movies hitting your favorite streaming service, including some high profile films just in time for the holidays. We’ve gone through and made a curated list of the best new movies added to Netflix , Prime Video , HBO Max , Hulu and more this month. They include a “Madden” biopic starring Nicolas Cage, a Netflix thriller starring Jessica Chastain, a pair of Oscar contenders and a new streaming home for “Obsession.” Rian Johnson is one of our best living filmmakers, and “Looper” is one of his very best films. This new film, based on a novel by “A Dog’s Purpose” author W. title: How 'Backrooms' Artisans Transformed YouTube Series Into Cinema’s Favorite Liminal Space Using 30,000 Square Feet of Sets and Four Sound Stages
summary: Backrooms expands from YouTube to large-scale studio sets, signaling opportunities in viral-to-film projects for adaptable performers.
content: Before Kane Parsons’ “ Backrooms ” became a $400 million global box office success, it was a YouTube series with 22 episodes, each ranging from two minutes to 45 minutes exploring the “Backrooms” lore. The series was a viral hit, and so was the movie. However, for the film’s production designer Danny Vermette and visual effects supervisor Ed Douglas, neither was initially aware of the series. After receiving a call from the film’s producer, Chris Ferguson, both Douglas and Vermette went down the rabbit hole and dove right in. Related Stories Gang Dong-won, Kim Go-eun to Star in Netflix’s 'The Twilight Between Us' From 'When Life Gives You Tangerines' Director, 'Queen of Tears' Writer Penelope Cruz to Star in and Produce Netflix Drama 'Patricia' From 'On the Fringes' Director Juan Diego Botto Speaking with Variety, Douglas, whose work is shortlisted for Oscar consideration , recalled his first response: “Is this real? Is this CG? What is this going to be?” After jumping on a call with Parsons, he learned about how the world had been built using Blender, 3D creation software used for modeling, animation, CGI, rendering, visual effects and simulation.” He says, “We started talking about what our process would be. Would this be a very traditional, film VFX process or would we bring in a hybrid process with the Kane Parsons Blender workflow? It was that combined process that we built.” Set in 1991, the film stars Chiwetel Ejiofor as Clark, a furniture emporium owner who discovers a portal in the basement of his store. Clark becomes obsessed with this alternate world, a never-ending series of liminal spaces lined with carpet and yellow wallpaper. Vermette spoke with friends who were familiar with “Backrooms” and Parsons. “I fast realized how versed Kane was in this universe, and how truly immersed he had been for several years and realized I needed to catch up with some of this lore and the theory behind how it works if we were to figure out a way to make this work and bu

title: Cult Hit 'Hundreds of Beavers' Returns to Theaters for Big Christmas Expansion
summary: Cult indie Hundreds of Beavers gets wider Christmas theatrical rollout, increasing exposure for its cast and creators.
content: It’s been four years since the cult hit “ Hundreds of Beavers ” first debuted and still two years since it started really gaining traction with wider audiences in 2024. But if it feels like the black and white, silent, slapstick indie comedy still hasn’t left the cultural conversation , that’s because in all that time it has continued to quietly play in theaters and attract audiences both loyal and new alike. Technically, “Hundreds of Beavers” has never left theaters. It continues to play individual screenings in a city or two every weekend. Now, though, “Hundreds of Beavers” is set to return to theaters for what is its biggest theatrical expansions to date. The film will kick off its third annual Northwoods Christmas, which will feature 130 screenings across 85 cities, with more to likely be added in the coming weeks. It came about after another fan campaign pushed for the film to come to some markets it hadn’t previously thought about or targeted such as Indianapolis and Charlottesville, and it will now play in everything from concert venues to microcinemas. Related Stories Cinematographer Caleb Deschanel on Finding the Right Techniques For ‘The Right Stuff’ Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’? The re-releases have become a holiday tradition for “Hundreds of Beavers,” which for all its wintery setting and its main character dressed like Santa, is being positioned as a new Christmas movie. The first time “Hundreds of Beavers” was re-released at Christmas 2024, which was shortly after the Blu-ray for the film became available, it brought in $118K at the box office in a month, and the producers continued the tradition in 2025. “There’s room for a Christmas tradition with the energy of a ‘Rocky Horror’ screening,” said producer Kurt Ravenwood. “You can watch ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’ and ‘White Christmas’ all you want, but for getting together with friends and family to laugh about the miserable winter ahead, ‘Hundreds of

Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in 'The Further Mis-Adventures of
 Cliff Booth'?
summary: Tarantino's new Cliff Booth installment sidelines Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate, hinting future adaptations may center on Booth.
content: [Editor’s note: This article contains small spoilers for “ The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth .”] It should come as little surprise that David Fincher’s “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” focuses on, well, Cliff Booth. The Quentin Tarantino -penned sequel to the filmmaker’s own 2019 Oscar-winning hit “ Once Upon a Time in Hollywood ” has always been billed as a spinoff following the continuing adventures of his fictitious (yet still iconic) stuntman Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt). But Tarantino has always loved building out his own shared and connected universe (s), and fans sure love exploring its outer limits. “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” and, by extension, “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” occupy a unique place in Tarantino’s cinematic world, as they’re both part of his so-called “Realer Than Real World Universe” and his “Movie Movie Universe.” Tarantino didn’t just keep crafting his movies-within-movies world with the hit film — he also introduced real-world (realer than real world?) elements and people (the Manson Family, of course, and all that entails). Related Stories ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ Will Come to the U.S. Next March ‘The Trip’ Returns for Fifth Installment, Next Sending Steve Coogan and Rob Brydon to Frigid Arctic Circle That bent continues in “Cliff Booth,” which is rife with both out-there elements and very real references (time for that “Hee Haw” resurgence, we guess). But the film also has to follow its own series logic, which means, yes, it’s the Cliff Booth show, but hey, where are our “Hollywood” co-stars Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) and Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie)? The project is the latest film from Deon Taylor and Roxanne Avent Taylor’s independent studio, Hidden Empire Film Group. Production is currently underway in Mississippi, with Maxime Alexandre (“The Nun,” “Annabelle: Creation,” “Crawl”) on board as the film’s cinematographer. Plot details are being kept under wraps, with filmmakers only revealing that the film “focuses on real-world trauma.” The “Don’t Open the Door” movie is also intended to launch a graphic novel-inspired universe that pushes the story beyond the screen. title: What Are Local Movie Theaters Showing for Thanksgiving 2026?
summary: Thanksgiving 2026 programming favors family franchises and prestige titles, guiding actors’ release strategies and holiday promotional planning.
content: One of the great things about going to the movies by yourself is that, technically speaking, you’re not alone. Even if you’re the only person in the auditorium, somebody thought about what you might like to watch, put it on the calendar, and made sure there was a place for you to sit. Earlier this month, IndieWire surveyed the programming at independent movie theaters across the United States on Election Night . Continuing that exercise over Thanksgiving weekend reveals another delightful cross-section of American film culture — albeit with considerably more cannibalism. Related Stories ‘All of a Sudden’: Why Does an 11-Minute Scene Centered on a Whiteboard Lecture Work So Well Onscreen? Watch ‘The Sheep Detectives’ VFX Supervisor Break Down the ‘Sheep-Isms’ That Made His Characters Stand Out At the Music Box Theatre in Chicago , where audiences have spent more than two decades celebrating Thanksgiving by singing along to “The Sound of Music,” moviegoers can also catch Ruggero Deodato’s “Cannibal Holocaust” late Friday night. It’s hard to imagine the Von Trapps sticking around for that one, but there’s something lovely about a neighborhood institution accommodating both crowds. In Seattle, the Beacon is observing its own Thanksgiving tradition with “Blood Rage,” the gloriously ridiculous slasher that made cranberry sauce an enduring point of reference for a certain subset of horror fans. For a somewhat more realistic depiction of the horrors of going home for Thanksgiving, SALA Event Center in Los Alamos, New Mexico , is showing Jodie Foster’s “Home for the Holidays.” In Cambridge, Massachusetts, the Brattle Theatre is celebrating Black Friday with a double feature of “Chopping Mall” and “Night of the Comet.” If you’d rather watch people die in a shopping mall than go to one yourself, that’s certainly an economical alternative. title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed to Saturday Due to Storm
summary: Weather delays move Macy's Parade to Saturday, shifting live performance slots and national TV exposure for talent.
content: Thanksgiving morning will not feature the Macy’s Parade this year due to extreme weather in New York, as the annual event — celebrating its 100th anniversary this year — has been moved to Saturday for the first time in its history. “The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration. Due to the expected severe weather, the 100th March of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will move to Saturday, Nov. 28,” Macy’s said in a statement to NBC News on Monday. “Our team is working through the operational logistics for this change and will share details as they are finalized. We expect the Parade to kick off at 8:30 a.m. on Saturday. Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.” Related Stories Alex de la Iglesia on His Upcoming Chilean Shoot ‘The Misunderstanding’: ‘Reality Has Become My Parallel World’ 'Big Mistakes' Season 2 Casts Randall Park, Debi Mazar, T.R. Knight, Jeff Perry The 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will now air live on Saturday, Nov. 28 at 8:30 a.m. ET/CT/MT and 7:30 a.m. PT. Peacock and Telemundo will also carry the delayed parade at that time. On Thanksgiving Day, NBC will instead rebroadcast the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones. Meanwhile, NBC is keeping plans to run a preview special, “Countdown to Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade,” on Wednesday night at 8 p.m. ET, hosted by Jack McBrayer (“30 Rock”). title: Gordon Ramsay to Host ‘Top Gear’
summary: Gordon Ramsay takes over Top Gear, signaling format changes and fresh guest opportunities for on-camera talent.
content: Longtime TV chef Ramsay is swapping hobs for hubcaps as he takes the wheel of the BBC ’s best-known motoring show. Ramsay, an avowed car fan who holds a racing license, has previously appeared as a guest on the show three times. “Top Gear,” which is produced by BBC Studios, will return in 2028 with filming to take place “across the U.K. and around the word” next year according to the studio, who promise more “epic adventures, daring tests and spectacular stunts.” Related Stories Netflix’s Hit French Action Thriller ‘Elite Force’ Starring Tomer Sisley Starts Production on Season 2 'Murder of JonBenet Ramsey' Trailer Puts Child's Parents Under the Microscope “My love affair with cars began as a child, growing up a field away from Silverstone, where I would climb over the fences and sneak in for a glimpse of the racing,” said Ramsay. “That early excitement sparked a lifelong passion for cars, motor sport, beautiful design and extraordinary engineering.” “At its very best ‘Top Gear’ has always been about the unexpected – surprising, entertaining and just the right amount of chaos. That’s the spirit we want to build on, bringing a fresh energy and ambition to create something truly thrilling for a whole new generation of audiences. It’s an incredibly exciting opportunity, and I genuinely can’t wait to get started!” The series ran from 1977 to 2022 when it was taken off air after co-host Andrew Flintoff, a former cricketer, was badly injured in a crash at the show’s test track. He suffered life-changing injuries after his open-topped three-wheeled car overturned. Earlier this year the BBC’s director of entertainment, Ed Havard, confirmed the broadcaster was planning to resurrect the show. Former “Top Gear” hosts have included Jeremy Clarkson and “Friends” star Matt LeBlanc.

title:
Lauren Ambrose on Playing the Mother of a Missing Teen in 'The
 Unbelievers' and Why 'Six Feet Under' Is a Hit with Gen Z
summary: Lauren Ambrose discusses portraying grief in The Unbelievers and the Gen Z resurgence of Six Feet Under aiding visibility.
content: Lauren Ambrose sounds almost embarrassed to admit that she was puzzled the first time she read the script for Nick Payne’s “The Unbelievers.” “I was like, ‘Oh my God, what is this? I don’t understand this at all,'” Ambrose told IndieWire, scrunching up her face in a mask of bewilderment. “What’s he getting at?” The drama, which is wrapping up its limited run at the Manhattan Theatre Club this month, is elliptical, moving backward and forward in time as it follows Miriam’s search for her missing son, Oscar. That description sounds like a thousand thrillers, but “The Unbelievers” resists easy classification — it’s a narratively daring story, overflowing with ideas about grief and faith and family. Related Stories ‘Paper Tiger’: James Gray Convinced Adam Driver He Was Playing the Hero, Then Crafted His Mythic End ‘All of a Sudden’ Review: Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s Long and Thoughtful Plea for a More Hopeful Future It was only after doing a workshop for the play that Ambrose discovered that what she initially found so alienating about “The Unbelievers” was actually its greatest strength. “There’s a lot to talk about, and a lot to parse, and a lot to think about, and it’s highly interpretable and analyzable, and I think that’s actually a marker of good art is that it can be interpreted in many ways,” Ambrose said over Zoom, hours before she was set to take the stage again. The role of Miriam is almost Everest-like in its difficulty. As the years pass without any sign of Oscar — not knowing if he’s been kidnapped or murdered or ran away — Miriam becomes more obsessed, more unmoored by the lack of resolution. That strains her relationship with her two daughters and Oliver’s father, who are processing their grief in different ways and worry that Miriam is growing fanatical in her insistence that he may still be out there. “It’s fun in a perverse way to go on this crazy journey every night,” Ambrose said. “There are all these wild turns. It’s tiring vocally. My body hurts, my neck

title:
'Paper Tiger': James Gray Convinced Adam Driver He Was Playing the
 Hero, Then Crafted His Mythic End
summary: James Gray shaped Adam Driver's arc by reframing his heroism, illustrating director strategies for guiding performance and narrative.
content: One night, after his second child was born, James Gray found himself up late watching C-SPAN coverage of the Global Economic Forum in Davos, and saw something he held onto for years. “This corporate CEO said, ‘95% of people don’t know there’s a game, and they lose,'” said Gray on IndieWire’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast . “Of the remaining 5%, 4% know there’s a game and don’t know how to play it, and 1% knows there’s a game and wins. And he said it with evident pride. I thought it revolting.” The CEO’s words hit home for Gray, showing a “cruel economic system that people can’t control,” where luck, timing, and “having skills that are popular at the right time” decide who wins. Related Stories ‘All of a Sudden’ Review: Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s Long and Thoughtful Plea for a More Hopeful Future ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Made Nearly $4 Billion Doing What Movies Can’t “I would love a system where everyone got rewarded, not one that picks winners and losers,” said Gray. “The idea of losers breaks my heart. The film was about my heartbreak over the world’s losers.” The script for “ Paper Tiger ” centers on three lead characters, each representing a different side of Gray’s cautionary tale about the dangers of chasing the American Dream. Of his three main characters, Gary ( Adam Driver ) is best positioned to be one of the “winners.” “[Gary] is the one person who knows the game, knows how to play it, and just [can’t] live with himself if he makes certain choices that might allow him to, quote-unquote, ‘win,’” said Gray of Driver’s character. “We don’t see that much in movies. We see people who are ‘bad guys’ who make the wrong choice, or ‘good guys’ who make the right choice and then wind up winning for it.” Gary, the ex-cop turned savvy businessman, presents himself as comfortable crossing that ethical line, but as the story slowly reveals, a strong moral code lies beneath Gary’s slick, tailored suit and wheeler-and-dealer image. title: TV Took the Wrong Lessons from the Success of 'Heated Rivalry'
summary: Networks misread Heated Rivalry's success, spawning copycats and narrowing casting opportunities instead of investing in original voices.
content: Many have classified the success of “ Heated Rivalry ” as an enigma, a phenomenon that burst out of Crave original containment and superseded even the most optimistic expectations. In early 2026, episodes averaged more than 10.6 million viewers in the U.S. alone. The show became the most-watched scripted title acquired in HBO Max history and Bell Media’s most successful original streaming series. There is a great deal of “right place, right time” to the success of the show, but is it possible “Heated Rivalry” wasn’t just the stars aligning, but a well-timed adaptation with all the right components that met an audience ready to buy in? With all its success, you’d think there are plenty of lessons to be learned from the show, but are the studios even listening? Related Stories Oobah Butler Wants to Expose the World’s Stupidest Industries, but They Get Worse Faster Than He Can Plan His Stunts Fixing Netflix’s TV Problem: 5 Changes the Streamer Should Make for Better, Sturdier, and Buzzier Series Based on the second book in Rachel Reid’s series “Game Changers,” “Heated Rivalry” follows competitive ice hockey rivals, curly-haired Russian Ilya Rozanov ( Connor Storrie ) and freckled Canadian Shane Hollander ( Hudson Williams ). Over six episodes spanning nearly a decade, the show follows the pair’s complex relationship as they compete as league rivals while beginning an adrenaline-pumping affair that proves more compelling than Stanley Cup wins. The show premiered in November 2025 to a modest audience, predominantly Reid’s readers, before word-of-mouth promotion boosted Jacob Tierney ’s show onto a global stage. First and foremost, “Heated Rivalry” clearly shows an appetite for LGBTQ+ stories . The series has been celebrated for its unabashed portrayal of queer desire between two men in an environment of deeply ingrained homophobia and rigid expectations of masculinity. title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Made Nearly $4 Billion Doing What Movies Can't
summary: Record-breaking GTA VI revenue highlights booming game sector and rising demand for performance capture and voice talent.
content: “ Grand Theft Auto VI ” took less than 24 hours to generate $3.79 billion in global sales . That’s roughly 15 percent of the year’s worldwide box office — in under a day. But Hollywood’s biggest concern about games might not be what else consumers are spending their money on. It could be just how many days, weeks, or even months people end up playing “GTA VI” instead of streaming movies or TV on other platforms. Even before Rockstar’s record-breaking launch on November 19, entertainment news outlets like TheWrap were asking whether the game studio’s historic release would seriously disrupt the attention economy . Several analysts echoed that concern in their own industry assessments, warning investors that the sprawling open-world adventure could monopolize living-room airspace until well after the holidays . Related Stories Frederick Wiseman’s Complete Filmography to Be Distributed by Janus Films Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing There’s a sort of delicious irony in realizing a game named after a felony has Hollywood panicking about stolen screen time. Personally speaking, as a former video game critic who now mostly covers film and television, I’m fascinated by the competition for both audience engagement and consumer interest. Still, that particular side of “GTA VI” discourse drives me up the wall. Games, movies, TV shows, and social media feeds do indeed battle for our attention, and the business of entertainment is ultimately all about influencing how strangers use their free time. Rather, the issue lies in the assumption that one hour spent with one type of story is automatically equivalent to another hour spent with an entirely different medium — and that comparing those numbers tells us a thing about what either is really worth. title: Lauren Ash & Mae Martin Among Cast Of Shozer’s Adult Animation High-School Comedy ‘Dirts’
summary: Adult animated high-school comedy Dirts assembles voice cast including Lauren Ash and Mae Martin, signaling upcoming voiceover opportunities.
content: EXCLUSIVE: Lauren Ash ( Superstore ) and Mae Martin ( Wayward ) have been cast in Dirts , an ensemble adult animated high-school comedy series for New Metric Media ‘s streaming service Shozer . They will appear alongside the likes of Ash’s Superstore co-star Mark McKinney , Mark Little ( Gary and His Demons ) and Ryan Belleville ( Workin’ Moms ). The show, set to premiere in winter 2027, follows Gus (Little) and Brus (Belleville), two deeply unpopular vegetable teenagers trying to survive life at Leguma Beach High, where high-society vine vegetables mingle with scrappy root transplants. The unlikely friends have to navigate the indignities of adolescence in a world where school politics can get particularly rotten. Related Stories Casting Lauren Ash, Mae Martin & Randall Park Join Crave Comedy 'Meatballs' News Samantha Bee Sitcom 'The Ambassador' Toplines CBC's Latest Slate Ash plays Sproutabella, Martin is Trevin Stems and McKinney Principal Corny. Also in the voice cast are Kyle Dooley ( Cupcake & Dino: General Services ) as Eggmilio and Butternut; Evany Rosen ( Total Dramarama ) as Cheryl and Snap Pea; Kayla Lorette ( Doomlands ) as Pep and Ms. Jicama; Rodrigo Fernandez-Stoll ( BlackBerry ) as Janitor McKale and Theatre Squash; and Chelsea Clark ( Ginny & Georgia ) as Gabe. Dane Clark, Viveno Caldinelli and Mark Montefiore co-created the show, with Caldinelli directing. New Metric Media is the producer in partnership with Little Black Stone Studios. Ariel Yang and Max Wolfond are the producers for New Metric, with Tysen Potter in the same role for Little Black Stone. Production will cater for vertical and horizontal viewing, and you can watch a first-look clip above. Dirts toplines the latest slate for Shozer, the YouTube comedy channel brand that Shoresy and Letterkenny producer New Metric launched last year. title: Takashi Miike’s ‘Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo’ From Neon Gets Early 2027 Release
summary: Takashi Miike’s Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo, starring Shun Oguri and Lily James, opens March 2027, indicating cross-border casting momentum.
content: Neon has dated Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo from Japanese auteur Takashi Miike for a March 5, 2027 theatrical release. The sequel Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo stars Lily James and Godzilla vs. Kong ’s Shun Oguri in a new take on the seedy and corrupt detective who first appeared in Abel Ferrara’s 1992 original neo-noir crime drama with Harvey Keitel as the Lieutenant. That was followed by Werner Herzog ’s 2009 film Bad Lieutenant: Port of Call New Orleans , starring Nicolas Cage and Eva Mendes. Neon acquired the U.S. rights to Miike’s third franchise outing that centers on a Tokyo cop (Oguri) steeped in gambling debt and a drug addiction and paired with an FBI agent, played by James, to search for a missing politician’s daughter (Liv Morgan) in Tokyo’s Yakuza criminal underworld. Related Stories Lifestyle Veruschka, Mesmerizing Supermodel of the 1960s and '70s, Dies at 87 TV 'Top Gear' Sets 2028 Return -- With Gordon Ramsay as Host The bad lieutenant and the FBI agent as they partner up are, without their knowledge, under the watchful eye of a crazed killer following their every move. The Neon film is written by Daisuke Tengan and is based on the original IP first produced by Edward R. Pressman. Japanese maestro Miike is best known for movies like Audition , the Yakuza trilogy Dead Or Alive and thriller Ichi The Killer , along with Sukiyaki Western Django, Visitor Q, 13 Assassins and his 100th film, Blade of the Immortal. Miike also has an upcoming slasher-horror film starring Charli xcx, Milly Alcock, Norman Reedus, Kiko Mizuhara and Show Kasamatsu. Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo had a world premiere at the Toronto Film Festival and will hit theaters on the same weekend as Pixar’s Gatto and Michael Jordan’s new take on The Thomas Crown Affair. The film is a US-Japan co-production, produced by the late Jeremy Thomas for Recorded Picture Company, Sam Pressman for Pressman Film, Naoaki Kitajima for Nippon TV and Misako Saka for OLM. content: It was a white Christmas on Wednesday as Beyoncé made a Houston homecoming in classic Texas style. Clad in all white, the 32-time Grammy winner rode into NRG Stadium on a white horse, performing “16 Carriages” and her cover of the Beatles’ “Blackbiird” to kick off her A Cowboy Carter Christmas NFL halftime show at the Houston Texans-Baltimore Ravens game. Taking the field with a group of white-clad dancers and marching band, Bey continued with her songs “Ya Ya” and “Riverdance” before she was joined by Shaboozey . She continued with “Sweet Honey Buckin'” and “Levii’s Jeans,” for which she was joined by Post Malone . Watch on Deadline Beyoncé then sang her version of Dolly Parton’s “Jolene” while sitting atop the back seat of a moving convertible, before taking the stage and singing her debut country album’s lead single. “Texas Hold ‘Em.” “I’m so honored to be in Texas right now,” she said. “It’s only right that we do ‘Texas Hold ‘Em’ for the first time in Houston, Texas on Christmas.” The artist was then joined by her daughter, 12-year-old Blue Ivy Carter , who joined in on the square dance choreo with her mom. Although Jay-Z didn’t join the family hoedown, Bey’s halftime performance comes after NFL commissioner Roger Goodell previously addressed the league’s partnership with Roc Nation amid the rape allegation against her husband. “We are aware of the civil allegations and Jay-Z’s really strong response to that,” he said at a press conference this month. “We know obviously that litigation is happening now. But from our standpoint our relationship is not changing with them, including our preparations for the next Super Bowl.” Jay-Z was accused of raping a 13-year-old girl in 2000 in a recent refiling of a civil lawsuit against Sean “Diddy” Combs .
